s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent depressive disorder with new onset of abnormal sensations in the upper limbs
salient_findings: New deep itching and creeping sensations in bilateral shoulders and arms
Sensations worse at rest, partially relieved by movement, and predominantly occurring in the evening
key_facts: 31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder
Depressed mood, anhedonia, nervousness, fatigue, decreased appetite, and poor sleep began 5 months after COVID-19
Previous severe episodes responsive to escitalopram and duloxetine
Intolerance to venlafaxine, bupropion, and trazodone
Mother had mania
Denied iron deficiency anemia, hypothyroidism, or substance abuse
Physical and neurologic examinations were unremarkable
Routine laboratory tests were unremarkable
New symptoms of deep itching and creeping sensations in bilateral shoulders and arms
Sensations caused night-time sleep disturbance
Escitalopram was discontinued and duloxetine increased to 100 mg/d
Clonazepam was reduced
Paraesthesias persisted despite changes in medication

shortlist.label: Akathisia
shortlist.why_kept: New onset of abnormal sensations in the upper limbs, worsened at rest and partially relieved by movement, is consistent with akathisia, a known side effect of antidepressants like duloxetine

shortlist.label: Restless Legs Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar symptoms of deep itching and creeping sensations in the bilateral shoulders and arms, worsened at rest and partially relieved by movement, could also suggest Restless Legs Syndrome

shortlist.label: Duloxetine-induced Paresthesia
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms began after an increase in duloxetine dosage, suggesting a possible association between the medication and the paresthesia

shortlist.label: Brachioradial Pruritus
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms of deep itching and creeping sensations in the bilateral shoulders and arms could also be consistent with brachioradial pruritus, a condition characterized by itching and paresthesia in the arms

shortlist.label: Notalgia Paresthetica
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms of deep itching and creeping sensations in the bilateral shoulders and arms could also be consistent with notalgia paresthetica, a condition characterized by itching and paresthesia in the skin of the back

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms, which are worse at rest and partially relieved by movement, are characteristic of akathisia, a common side effect of antidepressant medications such as duloxetine.

rejected.label: Restless Legs Syndrome
rejected.why: While similar, the symptoms are not limited to the legs and do not meet the full criteria for Restless Legs Syndrome

rejected.label: Duloxetine-induced Paresthesia
rejected.why: Paresthesia is a possible side effect of duloxetine, but the specific pattern of symptoms described is more suggestive of akathisia

rejected.label: Brachioradial Pruritus
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by itching on the arm, but it does not typically involve creeping sensations or worsening at rest

rejected.label: Notalgia Paresthetica
rejected.why: This condition involves itching and paresthesia on the back, which does not match the patient's symptoms
